chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadha', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Captives were brought to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). He ordered their execution but freed one man from among them. The man asked, 'O Prophet of God, why did you free me from among us?' He said, 'Gabriel informed me that God, may His Majesty be Exalted, said that you have five characteristics which God and His Prophet love: intense zeal for your family, generosity, good character, truthfulness of speech, and bravery.' When the man heard this, he accepted Islam and his Islam was good, and he fought with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) with fierce fighting until he was martyred.

key_terms.الغيرة الشديدة: Intense zeal or jealousy (in a positive sense) for one's family/honor

ai.seo_question: What are the five characteristics that God and His Prophet love according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the divine wisdom behind the Prophet's (SAWW) decision to free a captive, linking it directly to Gabriel's revelation of five specific virtues: zeal for family, generosity, good character, truthfulness, and bravery. This event underscores the Shia emphasis on the integration of moral excellence (*akhlaq*) and martial valor (*shaja'ah*) as indicators of true faith, leading the man to embrace Islam and achieve martyrdom. The hadith serves as a practical model for believers, illustrating how internal character traits manifest in external actions and divine favor.
